newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-KOZLOV GIVES RED WINGS 2-1 LEAD IN CONFERENCE FINALS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-KOZLOV GIVES RED WINGS 2-1 LEAD IN CONFERENCE FINALS.

text.p: Vyacheslav Kozlov scored twice and Mike Vernon made 27 saves as the Detroit Red Wings edged the Colorado Avalanche 2-1 on Monday to seize the lead in the NHL Western Conference finals.
Detroit's Russian unit, which has been sensational throughout these playoffs, came up big again in Game Three to give the Red Wings a two-games to one lead in the best-of-seven series.
The Red Wings, who have not won the Stanley Cup since 1955, are two wins away from returning the the championship round for the second time in three years and host Game Four on Thursday.
"This was their best game (of the series) and we won," Red Wings coach Scotty Bowman said of Colorado's improved effort over the first two games.
"We could have won all three. How do they like my Russians now?"

With the game deadlocked 1-1, Kozlov took a pass from Sergei Fedorov in the right faceoff circle and snapped a rocket past goaltender Patrick Roy for the game-winner with 11:40 left in the third period.
It was the seventh goal of the playoffs and second two-goal game for Kozlov.
The Avalanche had a chance to tie the game right after Kozlov's score but Vernon smothered Valeri Kamensky's slap shot from the far side of the right circle with 11:07 left.
Colorado almost tied it again in the final minute after pulling Roy, who finished with 26 saves, for an extra attacker.
With about 55 seconds left, Joe Sakic passed the puck from behind the right goalpost to Scott Young, who got off a shot from point blank range but it hit Vernon in the chest.
Kozlov had opened the scoring just 72 seconds into the contest with another assist from the swift-skating Fedorov.

Fedorov carried the puck to the bottom of the right circle, stopped and spun around, drawing three Colorado skaters toward him, before passing to a streaking Kozlov, who re-directed the puck past Roy from the bottom of the slot.
"We want to beat them so badly that we are right on top of the puck all the time," said Fedorov, whose team lost to Colorado at this stage in six games last year.
"Now I think we are starting to think we can beat them."
Colorado dominated the action in the first period, outshooting Detroit 13-8, but could not beat Vernon.
The score remained 1-0 until Sakic scored a powerplay goal 14:47 into the second period for his sixth of the playoffs.
Sandis Ozolinsh got the puck to Sakic, whose initial shot was blocked by Detroit centre Steve Yzerman. But Sakic picked up his own rebound and flipped a wrist shot over Yzerman and past Vernon.
Sakic was one of the bright spots for the defending Stanley Cup champions, turning up his game a few notches after sub-par performances in the first two games.
"We still didn't play with enough intensity," said Colorado coach Marc Crawford.
"They are playing desperate. We are not. Game Four is almost a must win."
